item.title: Roscommon and district league round-up
item.description: The severe frost won out last weekend with only a few games going ahead as planned. Moore United ended 2025 top of the Premier Division following a 1–0 win over Castlerea Celtic at a very cold Roscommon & District League grounds Lecarrow on St. Stephen’s night. The win comes almost exactly to the day the club was formed 50-years ago. item.title: Further cold weather could be on the way later this week
item.description: Further cold weather could be on the way later this week. It comes as weather warnings were extended across the Shannonside region today. A status yellow low temperature/ ice warning for County Longford and yellow snow-ice warnings for Leitrim and Roscommon were previously issued. They were due to elapse at 11 o'clock this morning but have now been extended. item.title: Four people died in work-related incidents in the region last year
item.description: Four people died in work-related incidents in the Shannonside region last year. The statistics have been released by the Health and Safety Authority. The HSA published provisional figures today showing that 58 people died in work-related incidents in Ireland during 2025. That represents a 61% increase on the 36 who died in 2024. item.title: Positive news for local towns in latest Irish Business against litter report
item.description: Roscommon town has risen to 11th in the latest Irish Business against litter report. It's a rise from July 2025's placing of 23rd, making it cleaner than European norms. Longford has regained it's clean status. The town dropped to 30th in July 2025's rankings. However, it is now ranked 22nd out of 40 towns and cities across Ireland. Local Roscommon Cllr Larry Brennan has commended those behind the town's appearance: Advertisement

item.title: Cllr concerned some local businesses may close in 2026 due to costs
item.description: A local councillor says he fears there may be further business closures in the region this year. Fianna Fáil's Seamus Butler believes the minimum wage increase and the auto-enrolment pension scheme may cause problems for local businesses. The minimum wage increased to €14.15 per hour at the start of 2026 which is the second highest in Europe. Cllr Butler says he's concerned some businesses may decide to close this year as a result of increased costs: Advertisement

item.title: Head of Ballaghaderreen Fire Station retires after over 25 years
item.description: The long-standing station officer of Ballaghaderreen fire station has announced his retirement from the role. Micheál Frain has served as a retained fire fighter in the area for 26 years. He took on the role of station officer 20 years ago. item.title: Environmental concerns raised regarding potential Co. Roscommon wind farm
item.description: Some environmental concerns have been raised in relation to a potential wind farm in Co. Roscommon. County Planners requested further information from Ballyfeeney Green Energy last month after they applied for permission to build six turbines between Scramogue and Kilglass. A decision on the controversial wind farm was due in December however Roscommon County Council sought more information from the developers - which has stalled the planning process. item.title: Funeral details announced for Longford man who died in crash on N4
item.description: The young father-of-five who died in a road traffic collision in Longford last weekend will be laid to rest on Thursday. 36-year-old Francis Kelly from Granard died following a three-vehicle crash on the N4 at Edgeworthstown on Saturday evening. Mr Kelly will be laid to rest in Granardkill Cemetery following funeral mass at St Mary's Church, Granard on Thursday morning. item.title: Funeral arrangements announced for Sister Brigid Reynolds
item.description: Funeral arrangements have been made for Sister Brigid Reynolds. Sr Brigid passed away on Saturday at St Vincent's Hospital in Dublin. She was 82 years old. Sr Brigid was born and raised in Finiskill, outside of Mohill and attend the Marist Convent in Carrick-on-Shannon. She graduated with a science degree from University College Dublin before entering the Marist Sisters Religious Order and being assigned to Kaduna in the north of Nigeria.
